events.title: Thomas Becket is murdered in Canterbury Cathedral
events.description: Four knights, believing they were carrying out Henry II's wishes, killed Archbishop Thomas Becket in his cathedral. Becket was canonised in 1173, and Canterbury became one of Europe's great pilgrimage sites.
events.html: Four knights, believing they were carrying out Henry II's wishes, killed Archbishop Thomas Becket in his cathedral. Becket was canonised in 1173, and Canterbury became one of Europe's great pilgrimage sites.

events.title: Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba routs the French on the Garigliano
events.description: After weeks of stalemate on the river Garigliano, Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba's Spanish army crossed by surprise and routed the French under Ludovico II of Saluzzo. After the French surrender at Gaeta, Spain controlled the Kingdom of Naples.

events.title: British forces capture Savannah
events.description: A British expedition took Savannah, Georgia, opening a new campaign in the American South. The southern strategy brought early gains but ended with surrender at Yorktown in 1781.
events.html: A British expedition took Savannah, Georgia, opening a new campaign in the American South. The southern strategy brought early gains but ended with surrender at Yorktown in 1781.

events.title: USS Constitution defeats and captures HMS Java off Brazil
events.description: In a three-hour single-ship action off the coast of Brazil, the American frigate USS Constitution defeated and captured HMS Java, a former French frigate taken by the British in 1811. Java had 426 aboard, the Constitution 475.
events.html: In a three-hour single-ship action off the coast of Brazil, the American frigate USS Constitution defeated and captured HMS Java, a former French frigate taken by the British in 1811. Java had 426 aboard, the Constitution 475.

events.title: The Treaty of New Echota cedes Cherokee lands east of the Mississippi
events.description: US commissioners and a small minority faction of Cherokee signed a treaty at New Echota, Georgia, ceding all Cherokee lands east of the Mississippi. Rejected by Principal Chief John Ross and most Cherokee, it led to the Trail of Tears.

events.title: Texas becomes the 28th US state
events.description: Nine years after winning independence from Mexico, Texas was admitted to the Union as a slave state. The annexation helped provoke the Mexican-American War the following year.
events.html: Nine years after winning independence from Mexico, Texas was admitted to the Union as a slave state. The annexation helped provoke the Mexican-American War the following year.

events.title: US troops massacre Lakota at Wounded Knee
events.description: While disarming a band of Lakota at Wounded Knee Creek, South Dakota, the 7th Cavalry opened fire, killing some 250 to 300 men, women and children. It marked the end of the Plains wars.
events.html: While disarming a band of Lakota at Wounded Knee Creek, South Dakota, the 7th Cavalry opened fire, killing some 250 to 300 men, women and children. It marked the end of the Plains wars.

events.title: Firebombs start the 'Second Great Fire of London'
events.description: German bombers dropped thousands of incendiaries on the City of London, starting some 1,500 fires. Much of the square mile burned, but St Paul's Cathedral survived amid the smoke.
